    Bug: Memory leak in Graphics destruction in v8 #10586

    New issue
    Copy link
    Closed
    #10835

    Description

    MattTreichelYeah
    opened on May 28, 2024 · edited by MattTreichelYeah
    Contributor
    Issue body actions

    Current Behavior

    Rapidly creating and destroying Graphics in v8 leads to a memory leak in at least Chrome, and eventually crashes with a RangeError: Invalid array length. Stack Trace:

    _initContext (GraphicsContextSystem.ts:255)
updateGpuContext (GraphicsContextSystem.ts:151)
addRenderable (GraphicsPipe.ts:109)
collectAllRenderablesSimple (buildInstructions.ts:87)
collectAllRenderables (buildInstructions.ts:71)
collectAllRenderablesAdvanced (buildInstructions.ts:142)
buildInstructions (buildInstructions.ts:47)
render (RenderGroupSystem.ts:116)
emit (SystemRunner.ts:74)
render (AbstractRenderer.ts:298)
render (Application.ts:155)
emit (TickerListener.ts:64)
update (Ticker.ts:461)
_tick (Ticker.ts:163)
requestAnimationFrame (async)
_tick (Ticker.ts:167)
requestAnimationFrame (async)
_tick (Ticker.ts:167)
requestAnimationFrame (async)
_tick (Ticker.ts:167)
...

    Expected Behavior

    In Pixi v7, this example is stable.

    Steps to Reproduce

    The following example reproduces it, linked here: https://www.pixiplayground.com/#/edit/3ocZP-9nVFphFe1ozWvsQ. Chrome's "Memory" heap slowly balloons and eventually crashes with the RangeError after about 15 minutes for me. Setting it to the latest v7 version and running it in parallel doesn't run into the same problems.

    If I change the destroy line to .destroy() or .destroy(true), it doesn't seem to make a difference.

    (async () => {
    const app = new PIXI.Application();
    await app.init({
        width: window.innerWidth,
        height: window.innerHeight,
    })
    document.body.appendChild(app.canvas);

    let rectangles = [];

    app.ticker.add(function()
    {
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
            if (rectangles[i]) rectangles[i].destroy({ children: true, context: true });
            const rectangle = new PIXI.Graphics()
                .rect(
                    0,
                    0,
                    100,
                    100,
                )
                .fill({ color: 0xFF0000 });
            rectangles[i] = rectangle;
            app.stage.addChild(rectangle);
        }
    });
})();

    Environment

    • pixi.js version: 8.1.5 (still an issue in 8.3.0)
    • Browser & Version: Chrome 124
    • OS & Version: MacOS 14.4.1
    • Running Example: https://www.pixiplayground.com/#/edit/3ocZP-9nVFphFe1ozWvsQ

    Possible Solution
